target: Sabtu depan kami mengadakan acara keluarga di rumah nenek.
english: Next Saturday we are holding a family event at grandma's house.

target: Kami ingin mengundang kamu ke acara syukuran rumah baru.
english: We would like to invite you to a housewarming celebration.
grammar: Syukuran = a small thanksgiving do for good news; syukuran rumah baru = a housewarming.

target: Kamu mau datang ke ulang tahun anak saya hari Minggu?
english: Do you want to come to my child's birthday on Sunday?
grammar: Datang ke + event or place = come to: datang ke ulang tahun = come to the birthday. The ke never drops.

target: Undangan pernikahan sepupu saya sudah sampai kemarin sore.
english: My cousin's wedding invitation arrived yesterday afternoon.

target: Mereka mengundang seluruh keluarga besar ke acara itu.
english: They invited the whole extended family to that event.

target: Maaf, kami tidak bisa datang ke acara kamu minggu depan.
english: Sorry, we can't come to your event next week.

target: Kamu jadi datang ke nikahan teman kantor besok?
english: Are you still coming to our coworker's wedding tomorrow?
grammar: Jadi before a verb checks a plan still holds: Kamu jadi datang? = Are you still coming?

target: Tolong balas undangan itu sebelum hari Jumat, ya.
english: Please reply to that invitation before Friday, okay?

target: Dia mengajak kami makan malam di rumahnya minggu ini.
english: She invited us to have dinner at her house this week.
grammar: Mengajak = casually ask someone along; mengundang = properly invite. Dia mengajak kami makan = asked us to eat.

target: Apakah kamu sudah menerima undangan dari keluarga Pak Budi?
english: Have you received the invitation from Pak Budi's family?

target: Kami mengundang tetangga baru untuk makan siang bersama.
english: We invited the new neighbors for lunch together.

target: Jangan lupa ajak suami kamu ke acara arisan nanti.
english: Don't forget to bring your husband to the arisan later.
grammar: Arisan = a monthly savings-and-social gathering; members pool money and one takes the pot.

target: Acara dimulai jam tujuh malam di rumah paman saya.
english: The event starts at seven in the evening at my uncle's house.

target: Boleh saya bawa teman ke pesta ulang tahun kamu?
english: May I bring a friend to your birthday party?

target: Mereka belum membalas undangan kami sampai hari ini.
english: They still haven't replied to our invitation as of today.

target: Kami akan mengundang kira-kira lima puluh tamu ke resepsi.
english: We are going to invite about fifty guests to the reception.

target: Datang saja langsung, tidak perlu bawa apa-apa.
english: Just come right over; no need to bring anything.
grammar: After a negative, apa-apa = anything: tidak perlu bawa apa-apa = no need to bring anything.

target: Ibu menyuruh saya mengantar undangan ke rumah tetangga.
english: Mom told me to deliver the invitations to the neighbors' houses.

target: Kalau kamu sibuk, tidak apa-apa, acaranya masih lama.
english: If you're busy, that's fine — the event is still a long way off.

target: Kami menunggu kabar dari kamu soal acara Sabtu itu.
english: We're waiting for word from you about that Saturday event.

target: Nikahan sepupu saya bulan depan di gedung dekat alun-alun.
english: My cousin's wedding is next month at a hall near the town square.
grammar: Nikahan is the everyday word for a wedding; pernikahan is the formal one on invitations.

target: Akad nikah dimulai jam sembilan pagi, resepsinya sore hari.
english: The vow ceremony starts at nine in the morning; the reception is in the afternoon.
grammar: Akad (nikah) = the short vow ceremony; the resepsi is the big party afterwards.

target: Mereka akan menikah di kampung halaman mereka tahun depan.
english: They are going to get married in their hometown next year.

target: Kamu akan memakai baju apa ke nikahan besok malam?
english: What will you wear to the wedding tomorrow night?

target: Banyak tamu memakai batik ke resepsi pernikahan itu.
english: Many guests wore batik to that wedding reception.
grammar: Batik is wedding wear: a good batik shirt is always right at a resepsi.

target: Kedua keluarga bertemu untuk membicarakan tanggal pernikahan.
english: The two families met to discuss the wedding date.

target: Adik saya baru bertunangan dengan teman kuliahnya.
english: My younger sister just got engaged to her college friend.

target: Lamaran mereka berjalan lancar minggu lalu di rumah calon mertua.
english: Their proposal went smoothly last week at the future in-laws' house.
grammar: Calon = future/-to-be: calon mertua = future in-laws, calon suami = husband-to-be.

target: Kami datang ke resepsi hanya sebentar karena anak kami masih kecil.
english: We only came to the reception briefly because our child is still little.

target: Amplopnya ditaruh di kotak dekat pintu masuk gedung.
english: The envelope is placed in a box near the hall entrance.
grammar: Wedding guests give cash in an amplop (envelope), dropped in a box at the door — not handed over.

target: Pengantin kelihatan bahagia sekali waktu memotong kue.
english: The bride and groom looked really happy while cutting the cake.

target: Mereka menikah setelah tujuh tahun saling kenal.
english: They got married after knowing each other for seven years.

target: Selamat menempuh hidup baru untuk kalian berdua!
english: Congratulations on your new life together, you two!
grammar: Selamat menempuh hidup baru = the set wedding wish: 'safe journey into the new life'.

target: Setiap acara keluarga, paman selalu bertanya kapan saya menikah.
english: At every family event, my uncle always asks when I'm getting married.

target: Mereka menyewa gedung besar karena tamunya hampir seribu orang.
english: They rented a big hall because they have almost a thousand guests.

target: Saya jadi panitia di nikahan teman baik saya.
english: I'm on the committee at my best friend's wedding.

target: Setiap tamu dapat suvenir kipas kecil dari pengantin.
english: Every guest got a small fan as a souvenir from the couple.

target: Fotonya bagus sekali, siapa fotografer di nikahan kemarin?
english: The photos are really good — who was the photographer at yesterday's wedding?

target: Orang tuanya menangis bahagia waktu akad nikah selesai.
english: Her parents cried tears of joy when the vow ceremony ended.

target: Setelah menikah, mereka tinggal sementara di rumah mertua.
english: After getting married, they are living at the in-laws' house for a while.
grammar: Mertua = your spouse's parents; menantu = your child's spouse. Rumah mertua = the in-laws' house.

target: Hari ini ulang tahun ibu saya yang keenam puluh.
english: Today is my mother's sixtieth birthday.
grammar: yang ke- + number = ordinal: ulang tahun yang keenam puluh = sixtieth birthday.

target: Selamat ulang tahun, semoga panjang umur dan sehat selalu!
english: Happy birthday — may you have a long life and always be healthy!
grammar: Selamat + noun makes a wish: selamat ulang tahun, selamat jalan, selamat makan.

target: Anak-anak menyanyikan lagu ulang tahun sebelum meniup lilin.
english: The children sang the birthday song before blowing out the candles.

target: Ayo tiup lilinnya dan jangan lupa buat permohonan!
english: Come on, blow out the candles and don't forget to make a wish!

target: Kami memesan kue coklat besar untuk ulang tahun ayah.
english: We ordered a big chocolate cake for dad's birthday.

target: Dia meniup semua lilin dalam satu kali tiupan.
english: He blew out all the candles in one breath.

target: Ulang tahun pertama anak biasanya dirayakan besar-besaran.
english: A child's first birthday is usually celebrated in a big way.

target: Jangan bilang ke ibu, pesta ini kejutan untuk dia.
english: Don't tell mom — this party is a surprise for her.

target: Kami menghias ruang tamu dengan balon warna-warni.
english: We decorated the living room with colorful balloons.

target: Teman-teman kantor memberi saya kue kecil di meja kerja.
english: My office friends gave me a little cake at my desk.

target: Umur kamu berapa sekarang? Jangan malu, hari ini spesial.
english: How old are you now? Don't be shy — today is special.

target: Nenek selalu memberi cucunya uang setiap ulang tahun.
english: Grandma always gives her grandchildren money on every birthday.

target: Tahun ini saya tidak mau pesta, cukup makan bersama keluarga.
english: This year I don't want a party; a meal with the family is enough.

target: Kado apa yang cocok untuk anak umur lima tahun?
english: What present is right for a five-year-old child?
grammar: Kado = a wrapped present (from Dutch cadeau); hadiah is the wider word for gift or prize.

target: Kami merayakan ulang tahun kembar mereka di taman kota.
english: We celebrated their twins' birthday at the city park.

target: Dia mentraktir kami makan bakso karena baru ulang tahun.
english: He treated us to meatball soup because he just had a birthday.
grammar: Indonesian birthdays flip the treat: the birthday person mentraktir (treats) the friends.

target: Lilin angka tujuh itu hampir jatuh dari kuenya.
english: That number-seven candle almost fell off the cake.

target: Kirim ucapan ulang tahun ke kakak lewat pesan singkat saja.
english: Just send birthday wishes to your older sibling by text message.

target: Pesta ulang tahunnya dipindah ke dalam rumah karena hujan deras.
english: The birthday party was moved indoors because of heavy rain.

target: Terima kasih sudah datang dan membawa hadiah untuk anak kami.
english: Thank you for coming and bringing a present for our child.

target: Besok kami mampir ke rumah bibi sebelum pulang ke kota.
english: Tomorrow we'll drop by auntie's house before going back to the city.
grammar: Mampir = drop by briefly on the way somewhere: mampir ke rumah bibi = stop by auntie's.

target: Kalau lewat Bandung, mampirlah ke rumah kami.
english: If you pass through Bandung, do stop by our house.

target: Kami menginap tiga malam di rumah kakek waktu Lebaran.
english: We stayed three nights at grandpa's house during Lebaran.
grammar: Lebaran = the Eid homecoming holiday, when the whole country travels to family.

target: Anak-anak paling senang menginap di rumah nenek mereka.
english: The kids like staying over at their grandma's house best.

target: Setiap mudik, jalan ke kampung selalu macet parah.
english: Every homecoming trip, the road to the village is always badly jammed.
grammar: Mudik = the big trip home to your family town before Lebaran — half the country moves at once.

target: Kami membawa tikar dan makan siang di halaman rumah paman.
english: We brought a mat and had lunch in the yard of uncle's house.

target: Sudah lama kami tidak berkunjung ke rumah saudara di desa.
english: We haven't visited our relatives' house in the village for a long time.

target: Nenek pasti memasak banyak kalau cucu-cucunya datang.
english: Grandma is sure to cook a lot when her grandchildren come.

target: Kami mengobrol sampai tengah malam di teras rumah.
english: We chatted until midnight on the terrace of the house.
grammar: Mengobrol = to chat; in speech you will hear it shortened to ngobrol everywhere.

target: Sebelum pulang, kami pamit dulu ke kakek dan nenek.
english: Before going home, we first said goodbye to grandpa and grandma.

target: Rumah sepupu saya jauh, jadi kami berangkat pagi sekali.
english: My cousin's house is far away, so we left very early in the morning.

target: Keponakan saya sekarang sudah bisa jalan dan mulai bicara.
english: My nephew can already walk now and is starting to talk.

target: Tante membuatkan kami teh manis hangat sore itu.
english: Auntie made us warm sweet tea that afternoon.
grammar: -kan can mean 'for someone': membuatkan kami teh = made tea for us.

target: Kamar tamu sudah disiapkan untuk kalian berdua.
english: The guest room has been prepared for the two of you.

target: Kami tidur di rumah saudara karena hotel di kota penuh.
english: We slept at a relative's house because the hotels in town were full.

target: Jangan lupa cium tangan kakek waktu datang dan pamit.
english: Don't forget to kiss grandpa's hand when you arrive and when you say goodbye.
grammar: Cium tangan — a child presses the elder's hand to the face — is the greeting for grandparents.

target: Kakek senang sekali melihat cucunya datang dari jauh.
english: Grandpa was really happy to see his grandchildren come from far away.

target: Kami membawakan nenek kain batik dari Solo.
english: We brought grandma batik cloth from Solo.

target: Setiap kali berkunjung, kami selalu pulang membawa banyak makanan.
english: Every time we visit, we always go home carrying lots of food.

target: Bulan depan giliran kami yang berkunjung ke rumah sepupu.
english: Next month it's our turn to visit our cousin's house.

target: Selamat atas kelahiran anak pertama kalian!
english: Congratulations on the birth of your first child!
grammar: Selamat atas + noun congratulates: selamat atas kelahiran = congrats on the birth.

target: Wah, selamat ya! Bayinya lahir di rumah sakit mana?
english: Wow, congratulations! Which hospital was the baby born at?

target: Semoga kalian berdua bahagia terus sampai kakek-nenek.
english: May you both stay happy all the way to being grandpa and grandma.

target: Turut senang mendengar kabar baik tentang pekerjaan kamu.
english: I'm glad to hear the good news about your job.

target: Semoga cita-cita kamu tercapai tahun ini.
english: May your dreams be achieved this year.

target: Selamat atas kelulusan kamu, kami bangga sekali!
english: Congratulations on your graduation — we're so proud!

target: Akhirnya kakak saya lulus dan langsung dapat kerja.
english: My older sibling finally graduated and got a job right away.

target: Semoga usaha baru kamu berjalan lancar, ya.
english: I hope your new business goes smoothly, okay?
grammar: Semoga + clause = hopefully/may: semoga lancar = hope it goes smoothly.

target: Selamat hari raya, mohon maaf lahir dan batin.
english: Happy Eid — please forgive my wrongs, outward and inward.
grammar: The Eid greeting: mohon maaf lahir dan batin = forgive my wrongs, outward and inward.

target: Selamat menikmati masa pensiun, Pak Hasan!
english: Enjoy your retirement, Mr. Hasan!
grammar: Selamat + verb blesses an activity: selamat menikmati = enjoy, selamat belajar = happy studying.

target: Bibi mendoakan pengantin baru cepat dapat anak.
english: Auntie prayed for the newlyweds to have a child soon.

target: Selamat jalan, hati-hati, kabari kami kalau sudah sampai.
english: Safe travels, take care — let us know when you've arrived.
grammar: Kabari (from kabar, news) = let me know: kabari kalau sudah sampai = tell us when you arrive.

target: Semoga tahun depan kita bisa berkumpul lengkap lagi.
english: Hopefully next year we can gather again with everyone there.

target: Kami ikut bangga, anak kamu diterima di universitas negeri.
english: We're proud too — your child was accepted at a state university.

target: Semoga lekas sembuh, jangan lupa banyak istirahat.
english: Get well soon — don't forget to get plenty of rest.

target: Turut berduka cita, ya. Semoga keluarga diberi ketabahan.
english: My deepest condolences. May the family be given strength.
grammar: Turut berduka cita = the set condolence, 'I share the grief'; the reply is a quiet terima kasih.

target: Jangan lupa bawa oleh-oleh kalau pulang dari Bali.
english: Don't forget to bring souvenirs when you come home from Bali.
grammar: Oleh-oleh = treats you bring people after a trip — coming home empty-handed is not done.

target: Kami membawa dua kotak kue untuk tuan rumah.
english: We brought two boxes of cakes for the host.
grammar: Tuan rumah = the host, literally 'master of the house': kue untuk tuan rumah = cakes for the host.

target: Ibu membungkus makanan untuk tamu yang pulang duluan.
english: Mom wrapped up food for the guests who went home early.

target: Apa yang harus kami bawa ke acara nanti malam?
english: What should we bring to the event tonight?

target: Bawa saja buah atau kue, jangan yang mahal-mahal.
english: Just bring fruit or cakes — nothing expensive.

target: Oleh-oleh khas Yogyakarta itu habis dalam sehari di kantor.
english: Those Yogyakarta specialty treats were gone within a day at the office.

target: Dia datang membawa martabak manis kesukaan anak-anak.
english: He arrived carrying sweet martabak, the kids' favorite.
grammar: Martabak manis = a thick sweet stuffed pancake, the classic treat to bring home at night.

target: Titip oleh-oleh dodol, ya, kalau kamu ke Garut.
english: Get me some dodol, okay, if you go to Garut.
grammar: Titip = ask a traveler to get you something: titip dodol = bring me back some dodol.

target: Kado untuk pengantin sudah saya bungkus rapi tadi malam.
english: I already wrapped the present for the couple neatly last night.
grammar: Object + sudah saya + bare verb = natural passive: sudah saya bungkus = I have wrapped it.

target: Selain kue, kami juga membawakan mainan untuk keponakan.
english: Besides cakes, we also brought toys for our nephews and nieces.

target: Nenek paling senang diberi kerudung baru warna hijau.
english: Grandma is happiest when given a new green headscarf.

target: Satu kardus mangga ini dari kebun paman di kampung.
english: This box of mangoes is from uncle's orchard in the village.

target: Jangan buka kadonya sekarang, tunggu sampai tamu pulang.
english: Don't open the present now — wait until the guests go home.

target: Oleh-oleh dari kami cepat habis karena banyak yang minta.
english: Our souvenirs ran out fast because lots of people asked for some.

target: Siapa yang membawa nasi dan siapa yang membawa lauk?
english: Who is bringing the rice and who is bringing the side dishes?
grammar: Lauk = the dishes eaten with rice; nasi dan lauk is the shape of every Indonesian meal.

target: Acara kumpul keluarga tahun ini di rumah kami, ya.
english: This year's family gathering is at our house, okay?

target: Kita perlu menyiapkan kursi tambahan untuk para sepupu.
english: We need to prepare extra chairs for all the cousins.
grammar: Para + person noun = plural group: para tamu = the guests, para sepupu = the cousins.

target: Ibu-ibu memasak di dapur, bapak-bapak memasang tenda di halaman.
english: The women cook in the kitchen; the men put up a tent in the yard.

target: Para keponakan bermain kejar-kejaran di halaman belakang.
english: The nephews and nieces play tag in the backyard.

target: Setelah makan, kami berfoto bersama di depan rumah nenek.
english: After eating, we took a photo together in front of grandma's house.

target: Tahun ini keluarga dari Sumatra juga ikut datang.
english: This year the family from Sumatra is coming along too.

target: Kami membuat jadwal kunjungan supaya adil untuk semua rumah.
english: We made a visiting schedule so it's fair for every household.

target: Grup keluarga di ponsel ramai sekali sebelum hari raya.
english: The family group chat on the phone is really busy before the holiday.
grammar: Grup keluarga = the extended-family chat group — every family has one, and it is never quiet.

target: Siapa yang menjemput kakek dari stasiun sore nanti?
english: Who is picking grandpa up from the station later this afternoon?

target: Acara sudah selesai, tapi para tamu masih mengobrol di teras.
english: The event is already over, but the guests are still chatting on the terrace.

target: Sisa makanan dibagi rata untuk dibawa pulang.
english: The leftover food was divided evenly to take home.

target: Sebelum pulang, kami memilih tuan rumah untuk tahun depan.
english: Before going home, we chose the host for next year.

target: Nenek berpesan supaya kami datang lagi liburan sekolah nanti.
english: Grandma told us to come again during the school holidays.

target: Rumah terasa sepi setelah semua saudara pulang ke kota masing-masing.
english: The house feels quiet after all the relatives went home to their own cities.
grammar: Masing-masing = each/their own: kota masing-masing = their own cities.
